thread:
anya (AE): Quick heads-up: Atlas Systems (prospect) asked for a perf POC next Wed. Their target: 450 sustained qps (chat gen heavy) with intermittent 20s spikes to 3k qps. SLA ask: p95 < 250ms, error-rate < 0.5%. Can we scope a run and an estimate?
diego (SE): Thanks. Workload mix? Single-turn chat or multi-turn?
anya (AE): Multi-turn sessions; avg input ~280 tokens, avg reply ~220 tokens. They also do embedding-based retrieval for ranking ~15% of calls.
tom (PerfEng): Given multi-turn, KV cache will matter. Proposed run: 15m linear ramp to 450 qps, 25m steady, then 5 spike windows (20s @ 3k) separated by 6m. Repeat whole run once for cold vs warm. Capture p50/p95/p99/p999 and warm-start delta.
rachel (SRE): Ops notes: 1) We'll need to warm the model KV cache and the retrieval cache. Plan a 10m prefix warm with representative prompts. 2) Dedicated pool warmup: provisioning takes ~7-9m depending on instance SKU. I'll request provisioning 30m before start.
deploy-bot: dedicated-pool-request(atlas-poc): queued -> provisioning initiating (est 8m).
diego (SE): For the load generator let's use k6 for multi-scenario clients (chat vs embed). Example snippet I'll share in the playbook. We'll simulate 600 concurrent VUs for spikes to emulate distributed clients.
tom (PerfEng): Example k6 snippet (simplified):
```
import http from 'k6/http';
export default function(){
  const payload = JSON.stringify({prompt: '... ~280 tokens', max_tokens: 220});
  http.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat', payload, {headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'}});
}
```
Include a separate scenario that hits /embeddings at 15% rate.
anya (AE): Atlas asked about cost during bursts — will bursts be part of reserved capacity billing?
sales-ops: Short answer: if they buy Dedicated with burst allowance we can absorb small spikes into the commit; otherwise overage pricing applies. For the POC we can apply a one-time credit to neutralize overage charges. I'll prepare a line-item estimate for hosted vs dedicated pilot.
rachel (SRE): Security flags from procurement: 1) need confirmation on KMS for customer keys; 2) encrypted logs at rest; 3) ability to isolate logs per tenant.
security: We'll need a formal reply but yes: we support customer-managed keys in Private/Dedicated, logs encrypted at rest, and tenant-scoped audit logs. We'll draft a one-pager.
tom (PerfEng): Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99/p999, token/sec, GPU utilization, request queue depth, proxy latency, model-infer latency, error categorization. We'll export traces and an OpenMetrics endpoint for Grafana.
diego (SE): Data setup: nya, can you upload 500 sanitized prompts and 200 retrieval queries to the shared drive? We'll use them as seed and randomize.
anya (AE): Uploaded: https://redwood.example/drive/atlas/poc-inputs (contains session sequences + retrieval keys).
rachel (SRE): Scaling plan: start with a single small pool (4 cards equiv), target GPU util < 80% at 450 qps. If observed sustained util > 85% during steady we scale to 2 pools. For spikes we'll rely on batching/backpressure and our short-burst policy; expect transient queueing.
tom (PerfEng): Important: include a run where KV caching is disabled to quantify retrieval overhead. Also run with cache TTL at 15m and at 1m to show sensitivity.
sales-ops: For the CFO, I'll prepare a simple sensitivity table: columns: sustained only, sustained+occasional spikes, always-hosted (no commit). Each row will show projected token cost and estimated monthly burn for a 3-month pilot.
anya (AE): Timeline: can we lock Wed 09:30 PST? Diego/Tom/Rachel available?
diego (SE): I'm on.
rachel (SRE): I'll be there and will kick provisioning at 09:00 PST.
tom (PerfEng): I can run the k6 scenarios and produce the results notebook.
security: We'll aim to have the one-pager by EOD Tue. Please ping if procurement adds new asks.
anya (AE): One last buyer question: will model weights ever be stored in their VPC for Dedicated?
rachel (SRE): For Private deployments yes. For Dedicated we can discuss private model hosting as an option; otherwise weights are in our managed infra. We'll note this in the security doc.
diego (SE): I'll include a short section in the POC report with an ops checklist: pre-warm, start steady, apply bursts, capture traces, post-run artifact bundle (.zip with results).
tom (PerfEng): I'll add visualization (latency heatmaps, GPU util over time) and a short `results_summary.md` for the buyer that highlights whether p95 < 250ms and cost delta for bursts.
anya (AE): Great. If you see this, react with :white_check_mark: and I'll confirm with Atlas.
diego (SE): :white_check_mark:
rachel (SRE): :white_check_mark:
tom (PerfEng): :white_check_mark:
security: :white_check_mark:
